definitions.definition: The young of certain animals, especially a group of young birds or fowl hatched at one time by the same mother.
examples: The brood of ducklings followed their mother.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The young of any egg-laying creature, especially if produced at the same time.
The children in one family; offspring.
(transitive) To keep an egg warm to make it hatch.
examples: In some species of birds, both the mother and father brood the eggs.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To dwell upon moodily and at length, mainly alone.
(intransitive) To be in a state of gloomy, serious thought; to think deeply and darkly, often with "over" or "on".
To hang or hover over something in a heavy, threatening way.
To protect (something that is gradually maturing); to foster.
